column1: # resources.tsv — the files 42 issues with a subject, other than the subject.
# WHY ONE REGISTRY. Each of these is 42's material, so the public template does
# not carry it and every student downloads their own -- and each used to be
# handled one file at a time: a strip rule here, an ignore rule there, a SKIP
# message and a doc paragraph each naming its own idea of where the file goes.
# They disagreed. shell-00's tarball was "in its folder" in one message (which
# a student reads as deliverable/ex07, a folder generate rebuilds) and "next to
# BUILD.bazel" in another; rush-02's dictionary was "wherever you like, the
# path is an argument" in the docs while the subject's one-argument form reads
# it from a fixed place in the turn-in (findings 016, 161). One row per file
# now, and everything that names it reads or is checked against the row:
#   the template build      strips it (the strip glob, outside tests/, plus the
#                           exact name anywhere), writes the ignore rule the
#                           template's .gitignore carries, a placeholder text
#                           file in the project folder, and a line on the
#                           project's SUBJECT-PLACEHOLDER.pdf;
#   tools/generate.sh       stages a harness file for the generators, refuses
#                           to wipe one saved inside deliverable/exNN, and
#                           names the path when one is missing;
#   tools/conventions.sh    checks that every file in named-in exists and names
#                           the path (the SKIP wording, the docs); that no text
#                           sends a student to "its folder" for one; that each
#                           consumer is a label in the row's project; and that
#                           the project's BUILD files name the file outside a
#                           comment, only in a glob with allow_empty = True or
#                           in a list of file names -- never as a label, which
#                           takes the package down on the template.
# A new project with a file of 42's adds a row here, and that is the whole job:
# the strip, the ignore rule, the placeholder and the checks follow from it.
# Columns, tab-separated, `-` for none:
#   project    the project folder, from the repo root
#   file       the name 42 gives it
#   path       the ONE path the harness and the student's program read it from
#   role       harness  the tests read it; it is never turned in
#              turn-in  it is turned in with the project; //tools:submit pushes
#                       it although the template's .gitignore keeps it out of
#                       commits (it is 42's, so a copy must not republish it),
#                       and the project's BUILD calls c_issued() for it, whose
#                       test fails at basic, worded from this row, while it is
#                       missing (tools/defs.bzl; //tools:conventions checks
#                       the call is there)
#   strip      git glob of the copies the template build removes, outside
#              tests/ (a copy under tests/ with the exact name goes too); wider
#              than the name where a copy may be renamed
#   consumers  the targets that read it, comma-separated: each SKIPs, naming
#              the path, while it is absent
#   named-in   the files whose wording must name the path, comma-separated
#   source     where a student gets it
# The placeholder goes in the project folder, never in deliverable/: that
# folder is what //tools:submit pushes, and a placeholder there would be turned
# in.
